question: What does FQDN stand for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fully Qualified Domain Name**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN)** is the complete domain name for a specific computer, or host, on the internet.
 
• It consists of the host name and the domain name, including the top-level domain (TLD), and can be used to uniquely identify a device on the internet.
 
• An example of an FQDN is **www.example.com**, where "www" is the host name, "example" is the second-level domain, and "com" is the top-level domain.
 
• FQDNs are important for DNS (Domain Name System) resolutions, allowing users to access websites and services using human-readable addresses instead of IP addresses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Domain Name System (DNS)** is a hierarchical and decentralized naming system for computers, services, or other resources connected to the internet or a private network.
 
• It translates more readily memorized domain names to the numerical IP addresses needed for locating and identifying computer services and devices with the underlying network protocols.
 
• DNS is an essential component of the functionality of the internet, as it provides a way to match names (a website you are seeking) to numbers (the address for the website).
 
• The DNS hierarchy consists of the root level, top-level domains (like .com, .org, .net), second-level domains, and subdomains.
